# The complete phase map of one `goose swarm run`

**Reference run:** `evals/swarm-bench/runs/nodeloop/baseline-n3-r3` — 3 nodes, all running the *same* base model under three LM Link aliases (`workhorse-`, `mihai-`, `gabee-qwen3.6-27b-fable-fusion-711…`), spec = `vendorsync`. 218 events, 121.7 min wall, final graded score **0.8157**.

**Driver spine:** `/Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/crates/goose-cli/src/commands/swarm.rs` → `run_swarm` at **:22542**.
**Execute engine:** `/Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/crates/goose-swarm/src/scheduler.rs` (main loop ≈ :2200–2585).
**Judge/pre-review contracts:** `/Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/crates/goose-swarm/src/judge.rs`.

The engine's own phase clock for this run:

| phase | min | % | mean node use |
|---|---|---|---|
| research | 4.6 | 3.8% | 3 scouts in parallel, ~1 lens lost |
| **planning** | **43.4** | **35.7%** | 3 serial rounds, 2 of them *discarded* |
| execute | 53.2 | 43.7% | 4.95 of 6 slots (82%) |
| gates (sink→finalize) | 20.5 | 16.8% | ~1 node; 2 idle |

---

## PHASE 0 — Boot, fleet reconciliation, pool resolution
`swarm.rs:22542–22960`

**What runs (no models called).** `strip_turn_context` freezes the operator's real spec; `reconcile_pool_with_fleet` builds the pool from what is *resident* (`lms ps`), not what is configured; `endpoint_model_ids()` (`/v1/models`) intersects it; `all_resident_unservable` (:2075) hard-aborts if the endpoint serves models but none of ours (the "LAN node dropped, every dispatch 400s in 2s" guard); `drop_unservable_devices` prunes the rest; a non-servable planner falls back to `fleet_pool.first()`. Then `planner_also_works` (default ON) pushes the planner in as a 4th device *if its model is not already in the pool*. Device capacity = `weight` (baked 2), so **3 devices = 6 concurrent slots**; `speed_weight` (substring map) orders routing. `dispatcher.spec_frozen` is captured **here**, before any model can touch the prompt (:22960) — delegation claims are made against the operator's bytes, not model-amended prose.

**Events.** `run_started` (:22845 — prompt, planner, pool, `gates{complete,goals,contracts,review,sink_review,smoke,delivery}`), `pool_resolved` (:22944 — the *true* worker list, because `run_started.pool` is emitted before the planner is pushed and under-reports node count on exactly the runs that add one).

**Failure modes / supervision.** Withdrawn alias → hard error before dispatch. Stale configured pool → overridden by residency. `allow_model_load` OFF by default, so the swarm never spins models up on its own.

**Node economics.** Zero compute. Correct as is.

---

## PHASE 1 — RESEARCH / SCOUTS
`swarm.rs:23056–23200` · banner "SCOUT"

**What runs.** `build_research_exts` assembles MCP lookup tools; `research_tools` reports whether the run can look *anything* up. With `research_scouts` ON (this run), `select_lenses` (:10274) picks fixed lenses (`edge-cases`, `architecture`, `libraries`) and `run_scouts` (:12781) fans **one lens per fleet slot**, in parallel, each bounded by `ScoutBudget{max_lookups:10, backstop_secs:900}`. Findings are joined into `research_findings` (reaches the architect + every detailer). `doc_prefetch` (OFF here) would forward only *grounded* findings verbatim to workers.

**Events.** `research_tools{available:[], can_look_things_up:false}` · `scouts_planned{lenses:[3]}` · `research_completed{findings:2, grounded:1, looked_nothing_up:1, lenses_returned:["edge-cases","architecture"]}`.

**What went wrong here.** Three lenses planned, **two returned** — `libraries` was straggler-aborted (`collect_fleet_with_straggler_stop`, :2896) and leaves no apology string, which is why `lenses_returned` exists. `can_look_things_up:false` (no `WEBSEARCH_BEARER`/`CONTEXT7_API_KEY`) yet `grounded:1`, because a *shell* fetch also counts as grounding (:8852) — one scout curled the vendor doc at `127.0.0.1:8931`, the other two reasoned from weights. **The spec explicitly says "read the API docs before you start"; two thirds of the research fleet did not.** The graded failures downstream (`sync_shape` 0/3 documented keys, `vendor_conditional` 0 ETag handling, `uses_max_limit` 0.03 — largest limit requested 3 against a documented max of 100) are all *doc-conformance* facts that a grounded fetch would have supplied.

**Node economics.** Genuinely parallel; 4.6 min for 3 nodes. **Extra nodes buy more lenses, not more grounding** — and lens count is capped by `max_research_questions` (4).

## PHASE 2 — SKELETON DRAFT VOTE (the best-of-N architect)
`swarm.rs:13186` (`parallel_plan`) · draft sizing :23389 · model dedup + cap :13397–13415 · emit :13568

**What runs.** `best_of_n = max(config, clamp(devices.len(),1,5))`, forced ≥2 when a floor is set → **3** here. Then the load-bearing line:

```rust
let draft_models = dedup(once(planner) ++ worker_models);   // :13397
let requested_n = best_of_n.max(1);
let n = requested_n.min(draft_models.len().max(1));          // :13415
```

`n` drafts run concurrently, round-robin over **distinct models**, each capped by `draft_timeout_secs` (480 default). `straggler_stop` collects as they land and aborts the last laggard after `straggler_grace`. `select_best_skeleton` picks the structurally best draft with a **pure-Rust scorer** (no LLM in the merge path); `plan_agreement` / `best_subset_agreement` / `structural_convergence` turn cross-draft agreement into `plan_confidence`.

**Events.** `skeleton_drafts{requested, returned, dead, straggler_aborted, secs, chars[], worker_count}` — self-checking: `requested == returned + dead + straggler_aborted`.

**The measured run:**
```
round 1  requested 3  returned 2  straggler_aborted 1  226s
round 2  requested 3  returned 3                       295s
round 3  requested 3  returned 3                       237s
```

**This is the single sharpest "extra nodes buy nothing" site.** The retarget ladder's only lever is *grow best-of-N* — it logged `best_of_n 3→4` then `4→5` — but `n` is pinned by `draft_models.len()` = 3. **Requested stayed 3 in all three rounds.** The ladder spent two extra full planning passes changing a number the cap silently discarded. And even when the cap does widen (more nodes = more aliases), each extra draft is another **sample of the identical model at the same temperature** — self-consistency, not diversity — and its only output is a scalar `plan_confidence`; the draft text itself is thrown away.

---

## PHASE 3 — DETAIL FAN
`swarm.rs:14180–14380` · emit :14345

**What runs.** Every skeleton subtask is detailed into an implementation-ready spec by one model call, `fanout_over_fleet_straggler` — **one call per fleet slot, work-stealing**, so a weight-1 node never queues two. Budget `detail_budget_secs` (420). `detail_memo` (ON) skips re-detailing a subtask whose *entire* input (goal+id+brief+files+findings) is byte-identical to a prior round. The system prompt hard-orders: use the owned file paths *verbatim*, and **carry through every external literal from research exactly** ("an endpoint off by a `/v1` returns 404 on every call").

**Events.** `detail_completed{task_id, secs, spec_chars, brief_chars, budget_secs}` on success; **`detail_fallback{reason: filler|agent_error|timeout}`** on failure — the worker then gets the architect's one-line brief as its *entire* spec (`is_agent_loop_filler` blocks max-turns filler from becoming a spec).

**The measured run.** 21 details across 3 rounds, 43–153s each, **zero fallbacks**. Round 2 detailed only 4 subtasks — `detail_memo` earning its keep.

**Node economics.** The healthiest fan in the engine: true work-stealing, ~2–3 min per round for 4–9 specs. Extra nodes shorten this linearly. But 13 of the 21 details belonged to the two rounds that were then **discarded whole**.

## PHASE 4 — CONFIDENCE RETARGET / REDRAFT LADDER
`swarm.rs:23940–24280` · `retarget_action` :10359 · stall guard :23700–23760

**What runs.** If `plan_confidence < ask_floor` (85 here), `retarget_action` reads the *binding signal*:
- `Agreement` + `can_grow_drafts` → **Redraft** (`effective_best_of_n += step`, `draft_temp -= 0.05`, `continue 'plan_loop` — a full re-draft **and** a full re-detail)
- `SpecClarity` + product undefined → **Ask**
- `SpecClarity` + open decisions + `may_research` → **ReResearch**
- else → **Ask**

`best_plan` is monotonic — the highest-confidence plan seen is kept, so a diverging redraft can never ship worse. `retarget_stall_guard` (ON) stops the ladder after `stall_tolerance` (1) rounds that fail to beat `best_conf_seen`.

**Events.** `confidence_retarget{round, binding_signal, action, conf_before, conf_after, detail}` · **`retarget_discarded{round, tasks[…]}`** — the full plan being thrown away.

**The measured run:**
```
01:42:33  retarget r1  agreement  redraft     conf 52  best_of_n 3→4   → 12 tasks DISCARDED
01:57:10  retarget r2  agreement  redraft     conf 61  best_of_n 4→5   → 12 tasks DISCARDED
02:10:38  retarget r2  none       stall_stop  conf 54 → keeps 61
```
Three skeleton rounds + three detail fans = **~30 of the 43.4 planning minutes**, whole-fleet, and the plan that shipped was **round 2's**. The last round's plan (conf 54) was strictly worse and was correctly rejected by `best_plan`; the ladder's net product was one plan two rounds old.

**Supervision.** `retarget_cap` (4), stall guard, `best_plan` monotonicity, per-draft timeout. What is *not* supervised: nothing checks that `effective_best_of_n` growth actually reaches the drafter past the distinct-model cap.

## PHASE 5 — CLARIFY / ASK
`swarm.rs:22090–22270` · emit :22130, timeout :22254

**What runs.** Still below floor after retarget → `ask_max_q` (3) questions written to `.swarm/clarify-questions.json`; interactive TTY gets `cliclack` prompts, everything else (evals, desktop, piped harness) gets a **blocking file handshake** on `.swarm/clarify-answers.json` for `ask_wait_secs` (default **1800 = 30 min**). Answers re-score spec-clarity; `answers_win_floor` (ON) prevents a later non-structural replan from throwing away a plan the user's answers just lifted over the floor. `ask_away` (OFF) would loop batches.

**Events.** `low_confidence_ask{plan_confidence, questions, open_decisions_total, open_decisions_not_asked}` · `low_confidence_ask_timeout{waited_secs, questions_unanswered, detail:"the fleet idled for the whole window and goose is now deciding these itself"}`.

**The measured run.** 3 questions at conf 54, `waited_secs: 5` (bench override), **3 unanswered → guessed**. One of them was literally *"Should `create_payment` be exposed via a public HTTP endpoint?"*.

**Node economics.** **The whole fleet blocks.** On a default desktop run that is up to **30 min × N nodes of pure idle** with zero work queued behind it. `open_decisions_not_asked` is the honest half — decisions past the cap are guessed silently.

## PHASE 6 — PLAN SHAPING (deterministic, no model)
`swarm.rs:13990–14140`

Applied to the winning skeleton, in order, all pure Rust:

| transform | line | effect |
|---|---|---|
| inject missing `integrate-verify` | :13566 | architect omits the sink ~sometimes; without it nothing runs the program end-to-end |
| `strip_integrate_verify_test_deps` | :2946 / :14016 | a failing unit test must never *block* the end-to-end gate |
| `split_fat_modules` (OFF) | :3196 / :14032 | slice a fat `hard` module so each child gets its own small contract stub |
| `relax_test_module_deps` (ON) | :2992 / :14048 | tests run parallel with the cli build |
| `relax_contracted_module_deps` (OFF) | :3113 / :14066 | flatten inter-module chains into a flat fan (needs contracts ON) |
| **`fan_verify_split`** (ON) | :3561 / :14081 | split the monolithic sink into one read-only `verify::<M>` per module + a **thin** join; the join gates behind *every* `verify::` even ones the architect forgot |
| **`fan_e2e_split`** (ON) | :3492 / :14100 | shard the end-to-end run by command into `verify-e2e::0..N`, sized to `worker_count` |
| `normalize_plan_files_to_package` | :14132 | amendment-safe path normalisation |

`e2e_oracle` (OFF here) would build the shard checklist from `spec_frozen` via `spec_advertised_surface` — the engine enumerating what the spec advertises instead of asking the model to remember.

## PHASE 7 — CONTRACTS FREEZE
`swarm.rs:24600–24760` · banner "CONTRACTS" · emit :24744

**What runs.** Non-test, source-owning modules only (a test module has no interface a sibling imports; freezing one costs a full worker-timeout call for nothing). `generate_contracts` fans one signature-only stub per module across fleet slots. Then: stray *files* the stub-gen wrote are deleted (a leftover stub would let a lazy worker ship it as "done"); `validate_contract_bundle` runs `ast.parse` on each stub; **`drop_unparseable_stubs` removes the ones that do not parse** — a module with *no* contract builds blind and the sink reconciles, whereas a module handed garbage writes against nothing while believing it has a contract. Survivors are injected into every worker prompt.

**Events.** `contracts{modules, frozen, injected, injected_modules[], validated{…per-module bytes/parsed/public[]}}` — `modules` is requested, `injected` is what workers actually received.

**The measured run.** `modules:4, injected:3 → [store, cli, meridian]`. **`api` — the largest module, later split three ways and later still the one that failed to compile — got no frozen interface.**

---

## PHASE 8 — EXECUTE
`swarm.rs:24928–25010` (wiring) → `scheduler.rs` `run_with_decisions` · banner "EXECUTE"

### 8a. Wiring (what supervises this phase)
```
Scheduler::new(devices, max_attempts=3)
  .with_sink / .with_doc_facts / .with_pause_file(.swarm/pause)
  .with_replanner(max_replans=1)      dynamic_replan default ON
  .with_judge(JudgeConfig::default()) GOOSE_SWARM_JUDGE  default ON
  .with_pre_reviewer(...)             GOOSE_SWARM_PREREVIEW default ON
  [.with_speculation()]               GOOSE_SWARM_SPECULATE default OFF
  [.with_degrade_on_stall()]          default OFF
```

### 8b. The dispatch loop
One central loop owns the `Dag`. Each pass claims as many ready tasks as devices have free capacity; a ready task prefers its planner-suggested device but **work-steals to the least-loaded free one** (`pick_device` :581 — least-loaded wins, then `speed_weight`, "the heaviest task went to the SLOW host; that is backwards"). A Claimed task holds its owned files, so two tasks never write the same file. Completions relax dependents, merge into `SharedContext`, free capacity, `notify_one`. Tick is **15s** whenever a judge / pre-reviewer / speculator / **replanner** is attached (the replanner's trigger — "nodes idle while a task is in flight" — produces no completion to wake on).

**Events per task.** `task_dispatched{task_id, device, model, attempt, deps, owned_files, context_slice_len}` → `rules_delivered{kind: implementer|test-author|read-only-shard|owns-nothing, kind_prompt, tailored}` → `task_completed{status, attempts, elapsed_ms, session_id, error, tool_calls[]}`.

### 8c. Idle-node mechanisms, in the order the loop tries them
1. **Replan** (`scheduler.rs:2313`) — fires when nodes idle with work in flight; `max_replans:1`. An *empty* answer refunds the round and records `replan_declined_at_incomplete` (an empty answer used to burn the whole budget and leave two nodes idle through an 18-min tail). Added tasks are **bonus** — their failure cannot fail the run. → `replanned{round:0, added:["web","verify-edge"], stopped:false}`.
2. **Judge** (`:2404`, `pick_judge_target` :1102) — **not capacity-bounded** (it must fire on a saturated fleet to free a stuck slot). Picks the longest-running Claimed task ≥ `min_age_secs` (90) under its intervention cap, `rejudge_cooldown_secs` 60, `max_interventions_per_task` 2, split capped at 1 per task. It first runs `deterministic_verdict` (no model): **BrokenCode** (owned file won't compile, judge.rs:356), **Accept** (files exist, pass syntax, untouched ≥ max(90,420)s — judge.rs:500), **Looping** (finalize-spin, :519). Only then, *if an idle device was claimed*, an LLM review.
3. **Pre-review** (`:2460`, `pick_prereview_request` :1235) — every *still*-idle node correctness-reviews a **completed-but-unreviewed** file-owning task. Multiple run concurrently, each on a distinct task, `pre_reviewed` marked up front.
4. **Sink review** (`:2504`, `pick_sink_review` :1275) — **default OFF** (`sink_review_enabled` scheduler.rs:47).
5. **Speculation** (`:2525`) — default OFF; races a twin of the longest chokepoint task, first-to-finish wins; fail-closed on owns-nothing tasks.

`IdleSlotGuard` (:305) is the sole releaser of an idle slot *and* the claimed device, on normal **and panic** exit.

### 8d. Judge events and what they actually bought
`judge_observed{elapsed_secs, tool_calls, thinking_chars, any_owned_written, owns_files, secs_since_last_write}` is emitted **before** every early return so it lands on *every* invocation. `judge_skipped{reason}` (`me_events_skip` :17554) names *why* a pass happened — four distinct paths all return `ok()` and were previously indistinguishable. `judge_verdict{verdict, confidence, hint, action, deterministic}`.

**The measured run — 43 judge verdicts:**

| action | n |
|---|---|
| `observed` (no-op) | **37** |
| `accepted` (deterministic completion) | 3 |
| `split` | 2 |
| `re_dispatch` (broken_code) | 1 |

Only **4 were deterministic**. Plus **11 `judge_skipped{no_idle_device}`** once the e2e shards saturated the fleet.

The 4 that mattered: `api` → split into `http-api-server`/`frontend-page`/`api-tests`; `meridian` → `meridian-client`/`meridian-tests`; `http-api-server` `broken_code` — *"vendorsync/api.py does not compile (IndentationError)"* → killed and re-dispatched, done in 71s. That one deterministic check saved the run. The 37 LLM "ok"s at ~45–75s each are **~35 node-minutes for zero state change**.

### 8e. Pre-review — the clearest discarded-signal case
`swarm.rs:17903`. Reads owned files through `review_file_excerpt` (whole file under 6000 chars; head+tail with an explicit `[middle elided]` marker above that — head-truncation here once *manufactured a phantom defect and shipped it as a mandatory repair order into the sink prompt*). One-line `STATUS|findings`, conservative. On ISSUES: writes `.swarm/prereview/<task>.json`. → `pre_review{task_id, device, had_findings, secs}`.

**The measured run — 9 pre-reviews, 2 with findings, both real and both specific:**
```
frontend-page: "last-sync display is never updated after a sync … the page still
                shows 'Never synced' instead of the actual last_sync time"
http-api-server: "_handle_summary must convert times to UTC before formatting …
                a payment stored as '…T12:00:00+02:00' is returned as
                '…T12:00:00Z' instead of the correct '…T10:00:00Z'"
```
Both are correct. Both were persisted. `read_prereview_findings` (:17297) splices them into the integrate-verify prompt (:20756) under *"CONFIRM each against the spec and FIX it before you finish"*. **Neither was fixed.** They gate nothing, drive no fix round, and appear in no verdict. This is exactly the "machinery is advisory, findings discarded" pattern.

### 8f. Execute occupancy — measured
EXECUTE window 3190s. Integrating in-flight tasks over that window: **mean concurrency 4.95 against 6 slots = 82%**. Time spent at ≤3 concurrent tasks: **189s of 3190**.

```
concurrency:   2    3     4     5    6    7    8
seconds:      60  129  1181   948  450  261  161
```

**EXECUTE is not where the idle is.** The binding constraint is *DAG width*, not node count — and DAG width is decided by the architect in Phase 2. Adding nodes here adds slots the plan has no tasks for.

### 8g. Supervision inventory for EXECUTE
`worker_timeout_secs` 420 · `max_attempts` 3 · `progress_watchdog_secs` 900 (continuous thinking-only; a real tool call resets it) · `spiral_break_chars` 12000 · `repeat_break` (`repeat_call_hash`) · `stream_decode_retry` · file-hold mutual exclusion · judge-kill exclusion from the retry budget (`n.attempts - judge_kills >= max_attempts`, scheduler.rs:977 — a judge kill must not burn a task's transient-retry budget) · `salvage_spin` ON (a spin-failed non-test task that already wrote its file becomes Done, so the sink is the real gate) · `.swarm/pause` sentinel.

## PHASE 9 — THE `verify::` LAYER
Generated by `fan_verify_split` (:3561), spec by `per_module_verify_spec` (:15671).

**What runs.** One `verify::<M>` per file-owning non-test module. **Owns nothing, writes nothing** — `rules_delivered{kind:"read-only-shard"}`. `depends_on: [M]` and **nothing else** — never a test task: a version that added an edge onto the test-writer deadlocked the oracle (`test-wal` SyntaxError → `fail_descendants` → `verify::wal` → integrate-verify never ran at all).

**The measured run.** `verify::store` 107s, `verify::cli` 48s, `verify::api` 140s, `verify::meridian` 145s — each dispatched the instant its module completed, spread across all three devices. **This is a genuinely fleet-parallel correctness layer and it works.**

**Where nodes could buy correctness.** These are read-only shards on completed code — the perfect shape for redundancy. Today each module gets **exactly one** verifier and its verdict gates nothing beyond the sink's dependency edge.

---

## PHASE 10 — `verify-e2e::` SHARDS
`fan_e2e_split` (:3492), shard spec `e2e_shard_spec` (:3428).

**What runs.** The whole-program run is sharded by command into `verify-e2e::0..N`, `N = worker_count`, each read-only, each depending on **all** `verify::` tasks. `integrate-verify` then *joins* them instead of running every command itself. With `e2e_oracle` ON the shard checklist is enumerated by the engine from `spec_frozen` (`spec_advertised_surface`); OFF (this run) it comes from the model.

**The measured run.** All 3 dispatched at 02:47:46; completed at 493s / 615s / 283s. But device placement put **two shards on `gabee` and one on `workhorse`, leaving `mihai` free** — `pick_device` is least-loaded-first, and `mihai` was still holding `web`. From this moment on, every judge call logged `no_idle_device`.

---

## PHASE 11 — `integrate-verify` (the sink)
Thin spec `thin_integrate_verify_spec` (:15716) under fan-verify; full `joined_integrate_verify_spec` (:15699) otherwise.

**What runs.** One task, `rules_delivered{kind:"owns-nothing"}`, `sink_max_turns` 120, prompt pre-loaded with `read_prereview_findings` output. Budget = `scaled_sink_cap(sink_cap_secs=1800, tree_bytes, ref_bytes=30000)` (:1106) — scaled **by delivered tree bytes, clamped ×1.0–2.0**, because a fixed ceiling truncates the join more surely the more a run produced (baseline-n3-r0's join was cut at exactly 1800s mid-repair and then scored 0.00 on tier-A `sync_shape`); the 2× clamp still cuts the known 4326s pathological loop. C1: because the sink **owns nothing**, its failure is a *model self-report* and is excluded from the green-blocking set — only a file-owning task can block green.

**The measured run.** Dispatched 02:58:01 the moment the last shard landed; done 03:06:20 — **499 seconds solo, two of three nodes idle**, and this is the phase that decides whether the app ships. `sink_review` — the mechanism built for exactly this window — is **default OFF at both ends** (`scheduler.rs:47`; the producer and the consumer once disagreed, so every run *reported* `sink_review: true` while the queue was never filled).

---

## PHASE 12 — COMPLETE / verify-fix tail
`swarm.rs:25010–25800` · banner "COMPLETE"

**What runs, per round (`complete_rounds` 2, i.e. up to 3 verifies + 2 fixes), capped by `complete_cap_secs`:**

| check | line | gate | this run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_smoke_gate` (pytest collect + `pytest -q` + entry `--help`) | :15235 | **hard** | `pytest -q` FAILED |
| failed-task findings (non-bonus, owns-something) | :25090 | only when smoke is *blind* | — |
| `missing_source_deliverables` re-stat'd each round | :25150 | hard | 0 |
| `cross_module_drift` | :25194 | hard | `checked:9, findings:0` |
| `http_timeout_scan` | :25255 | hard | *(post-dates this log — added at 936a66edd)* |
| `run_spec_contract` | :25295 | hard | `verified:0, findings:0, inconclusive:1` — **has never concluded on this bench** |
| `run_pillar_checks` | :25320 | **advisory only** | goals OFF |

`complete_verify{round, ran, passed, findings, finding_texts[]}` carries `elide_middle(f, 150, 650)` — head-light, tail-heavy, because *the error is the only actionable part* (a pytest failure was once recorded as a list of collected tests, the banner starting one char past the old cut).

**The fix step — two paths:**
- **Default (this run): serial.** One fix on `smoke_fix_target` = the highest-`speed_weight` enabled device (this path used to ignore speed weights entirely and land every repair on the slowest node). Wrapped in `timeout(fix_cap_secs)`; partial writes stay on the real tree.
- **`GOOSE_SWARM_SPEC_REPAIR` (default OFF, :22353): the twin race.** One independent attempt **per fleet model**, each in its own shadow (`cp -r`), each owning *every* app file, then a **deterministic re-verify of every shadow with the same `run_smoke_gate`** and `pick_repair_winner` promotes only a twin that **beats** the baseline finding count. A twin whose gate could not run scores `None` and can never win. Crucially it grades **the tree, not the agent's exit** — a corpus sweep of 90 logs found three historical rounds that went red→green on an agent killed at the cap.

**The measured tail:**
```
03:06:34  complete_verify r0  ran:true  passed:false  findings:1   (pytest -q failed)
03:06:34  complete_fix_dispatched  twin:0  path:"serial"
03:26:34  complete_fix_completed   secs:1200  agent_ok:false  verified_findings:null
03:26:49  complete_verify r1  passed:false  findings:1  (same failure)
03:26:49  complete_result{passed:false, verified:false, remaining_findings:1}
```
**1200 seconds — the full `fix_cap` — on one node, with two nodes idle, producing nothing.** The mechanism that would have raced three twins and picked the winner by oracle was one env var away and off.

---

## PHASE 13 — Finalize
`swarm.rs:25960–26420`

- `sink_review` drain (:25969) — `drain_sink_review()` then `verify_finding` re-checks each against the **final** tree, fail-closed, and emits `sink_review{prewarmed, survivors, refuted}`. **Advisory; drives no fix.** Never fired (lever OFF).
- `orphan_files` (:26046) — source files on disk no task owns, with a `is_stub_content` flag. Never deletes. → `{count:1, files:[{tests/test_edge_cases.py, stub:false}]}`.
- `review` (:26089) — the model-free AST wiring reviewer, diffed against a **pre-EXECUTE snapshot** so only findings *this run introduced* can act. `app_scope_py` cap violations print `SCAN CAPPED … PARTIAL, not clean, and cannot demote`. → `{ran:true, modules:9, findings:[]}`.
- `run_overview` (:26265/:26328) — a grounded summary agent reading real code excerpts, **forbidden** from any works/tested/verified claim and `scrub_overclaim`'d anyway. **Skipped on a red build** → this run emitted `generated:false`. Must run *before* `run_finished` because the desktop `kill_on_drop`-kills the CLI the instant it reads final stdout.
- `run_finished{report, phases}` (:26375) — `phases` gains `dispatch_occupancy_*` only when `occupancy_on()` (OFF here).

**Scoring is external** (`evals/swarm-bench` → `verdict.json`, `scorer_version: sb-3`): weighted tiers A .25 / B .30 / C .25 / D .20. This run: **0.8157** (A .8333, B .875, C .8571, D .653).

## The node-second ledger

Whole run: 7302s × 3 devices = **21,906 node-seconds available**. The scheduler's own `busy_ms` (which counts *only* scheduler-dispatched worker tasks — not drafts, details, contracts, judge calls, pre-reviews, or the repair tail) sums to **4,753s**. There is no occupancy instrument at all for the 64 minutes of research + planning + gates.

Named idle windows in this one run:

| window | duration | idle nodes | node-seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| skeleton draft rounds 2 & 3 + their detail fans (discarded whole) | ~1770s | — | **~30 fleet-minutes producing a plan that was rejected** |
| clarify ask (5s here; **1800s default**) | 5s | 3 | 15 (default: 5,400) |
| `integrate-verify` solo | 499s | 2 | ~1,000 |
| `complete-fix` serial | 1200s | 2 | ~2,400 |
| judge LLM "observed" no-ops | 37 calls × ~60s | — | ~2,200 spent, 0 state changes |

# The 5 highest-leverage conversions of idle node-seconds into verified quality

Ranked by (node-seconds available) × (probability the seconds change a graded check) ÷ (risk).

### 1. Turn the repair tail into the twin race — `GOOSE_SWARM_SPEC_REPAIR=1`
`swarm.rs:25460–25620`. This is **already built and is the only mechanism in the engine that implements the reframe end to end**: N nodes → N independent attempts → **a deterministic oracle picks the winner** → a twin lands *only* if its re-verify beats the baseline. It grades the tree, not the agent. In this run it would have converted 2,400 wasted idle node-seconds into 3 graded attempts at the one finding that held the app red. Risk is bounded by construction: shadow isolation, `pick_repair_winner` requires a strict improvement, and a shadow whose gate could not run scores `None` and can never promote. **Zero-code change, highest expected value.** Pair with `GOOSE_SWARM_COMPLETE_ROUNDS≥3` so a winning twin gets a second round.

### 2. Make pre-review findings *gate*, not narrate
`swarm.rs:17903` produces them; `:20756` splices them into a prompt; nothing consumes the outcome. Both findings in this run were real, specific, file-and-line concrete, and both shipped unfixed. The fix is structural, not more prompting: route `.swarm/prereview/*.json` into `verdict.findings` in the COMPLETE loop **behind the same `verify_finding` fail-closed re-check the sink-review drain already uses** (:25980) — so a stale or over-read finding is refuted and dropped, and a surviving one drives a fix round. This is where extra nodes buy correctness *directly*: pre-review is a per-completed-task read-only job, so **K nodes = K independent reviewers per module**, and requiring 2-of-K agreement before a finding is promoted turns cheap redundancy into precision. It is the single mechanism whose output is already correct and simply not wired to anything.

### 3. Turn `verify::<M>` into a real multi-verifier vote (and give the fleet the whole verify layer)
`fan_verify_split` (:3561) already produces the perfect shape — read-only, owns-nothing, fans like build tasks, one per module, dependent only on its own module. Today each module gets **one** verifier whose verdict gates only a dependency edge. Emit `verify::<M>::0..K` for K free slots with **different lenses** (contract conformance / edge cases / the spec's advertised surface), and promote a finding when ≥2 lenses agree. Turn `GOOSE_SWARM_E2E_ORACLE=1` at the same time so the e2e shards check what `spec_frozen` **advertises** rather than what the model remembers — that is the engine, not a model, deciding what "correct" means. Every failing graded check in this run (`sync_shape` 0/3 documented keys, `vendor_conditional`, `uses_max_limit` 3-vs-100, `client_timeouts`) is a **spec-conformance** defect that a spec-enumerated verifier can name deterministically.

### 4. Stop paying for a redraft ladder that cannot widen — spend those rounds on grounding instead
`swarm.rs:13415` caps drafts at `draft_models.len()`; the ladder logged `best_of_n 3→4→5` while requesting **3, 3, 3**. Two full fleet-wide planning rounds (~30 min) produced a plan that was then discarded, and the winner was two rounds old. Either (a) make the cap visible to `retarget_action` so `can_grow_drafts` is false once `effective_best_of_n ≥ draft_models.len()` — the ladder then correctly routes to **Ask** or **ReResearch** instead of re-rolling the identical dice; or (b) drop `retarget_rounds` to 1 and put the reclaimed 30 fleet-minutes into **grounded research**: this run had `can_look_things_up:false`, one of three lenses grounded, and the spec's own instruction ("read the API docs first") went unfollowed — while the whole failing tier of the grade is doc conformance. Also note the ladder's redraft rounds are **serial**: extra nodes make each round marginally wider and never make the ladder shorter.

### 5. Fill the sink and the ask windows — `GOOSE_SWARM_SINK_REVIEW=1`, and never block N nodes on an unanswered question
`pick_sink_review` (scheduler.rs:1275) exists precisely because *"the SINK owns 100% of the solo time in 2 of 3 measured runs (543–1045s with two nodes idle). It has never run once."* This run's sink was 499s solo. Turning it on costs nothing in delivered quality — the findings are re-verified fail-closed against the **final post-sink tree** (:25980) before anyone sees them — but today the survivors are still **advisory**; combined with fix #2 they should feed the same gated findings channel. Separately, the clarify ask blocks the **entire fleet** for up to `ask_wait_secs` (**1800s default**) with nothing dispatched: the idle nodes should be doing sink-style dimension reviews, or pre-computing the alternative plans for each candidate answer, instead of sleeping. And `open_decisions_not_asked` (3 asked of N, remainder **guessed**) is a place where an idle node could at least *research* the guess rather than invent it.

---

## Two structural observations that frame all five

**Every node runs the same model.** The three devices are `workhorse-`, `mihai-`, `gabee-` aliases of `qwen3.6-27b-fable-fusion-711`. So N nodes = **N samples of one distribution**, not N opinions. Everywhere the engine treats extra nodes as *diversity* (the skeleton agreement vote, the LLM judge's second opinion) it is measuring sampling noise and converting it into a scalar it then discards. Everywhere it treats extra nodes as **independent attempts graded by a deterministic oracle** (the twin race, the shadow re-verify, `pick_repair_winner`) it gets real best-of-N — which is precisely the mechanism strong models are approximated by. Findings F405's identical 3-node/1-node scores are the direct consequence: the fleet's 2.5× throughput is spent on the first kind of mechanism, not the second.

**The engine already knows the difference.** `pick_repair_winner`, `run_smoke_gate` on a shadow root, `drop_unparseable_stubs`, `spec_advertised_surface`, `verify_finding`'s fail-closed re-check, `cross_module_drift`, `http_timeout_scan`, the AST wiring review — every one of these is *engine truth, not a model claim*, and every one is either default-OFF, advisory, or single-instance. The conversion the reframe asks for is not new machinery. It is **routing the existing deterministic oracles across the idle nodes, and letting their verdicts gate.**
